title.zh: 卷一百〇四 列傳第三十四: 文學下
title.raw: 卷一百〇四 列傳第三十四: 文學下 Volume 104 Biographies 34: Literature 2

sentences.zh: 文學下 ○王鼎耶律昭劉輝耶律孟簡耶律谷欲

translations.literal: Literature (Part 2) ○ Wang Ding, Yelü Zhao, Liu Hui, Yelü Mengjian, Yelü Guyu
translations.idiomatic: Literature (Part 2) — Wang Ding, Yelü Zhao, Liu Hui, Yelü Mengjian, and Yelü Guyu

sentences.zh: 王鼎，字虛中，涿州人。

translations.literal: Wang Ding, style name Xuzhong, was a man of Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ding, whose courtesy name was Xuzhong, came from Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 幼好學，居太寧山數年，博通經史。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning; he dwelt on Mount Taining for several years and attained thorough mastery of the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he loved study; he lived on Mount Taining for years until he had mastered the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 時馬唐俊有文名燕、薊間，適上巳，與同志祓禊水濱，酌酒賦詩。

translations.literal: At that time Ma Tangjun had a literary reputation between Yan and Ji; it happened to be the Shangsi Festival, and with like-minded friends he performed the spring purification rite by the waterside, pouring wine and composing poetry.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Ma Tangjun enjoyed a literary reputation in the Yan and Ji region. It chanced to be the Shangsi Festival, and he went with friends to perform the spring purification by the water, drinking wine and composing verse.

sentences.zh: 鼎偶造席，唐俊見鼎樸野，置下坐。

translations.literal: Ding happened by the gathering; Tangjun saw that Ding was plain and rustic and seated him in the lowest place.
translations.idiomatic: Ding happened upon the gathering. Tangjun took him for a rustic and gave him the lowest seat.

sentences.zh: 欲以詩困之，先出所作索賦，鼎援筆立成。

translations.literal: Wishing to embarrass him with poetry, he first presented his own composition and demanded a matching piece; Ding took up the brush and completed it at once.
translations.idiomatic: Intending to trap him with verse, Tangjun first produced his own poem and demanded a reply; Ding took up the brush and finished one on the spot.

sentences.zh: 唐俊驚其敏妙，因與定交。

translations.literal: Tangjun marveled at his quick brilliance and therefore formed a sworn friendship with him.
translations.idiomatic: Tangjun was astonished by his quick wit and thereupon became his sworn friend.

sentences.zh: 清寧五年，擢進士第。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qingning he was selected in the jinshi examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Qingning reign he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 調易州觀察判官，改淶水縣令，累遷翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was assigned as judicial aide to the Yizhou Observation Commission, then transferred to magistrate of Lianshui County, and was repeatedly promoted to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as judicial aide on the Yizhou Observation Commission, then made magistrate of Lianshui County, and rose in time to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 當代典章多出其手。

translations.literal: Most of the ritual regulations of the age issued from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the age's ritual codes and statutes came from his pen.

sentences.zh: 上書言治道十事，帝以鼎達政體，事多咨訪。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial setting forth ten matters of governance; the emperor considered Ding well versed in statecraft and frequently consulted him on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne on ten points of governance. The emperor judged Ding thoroughly versed in statecraft and often sought his counsel.

sentences.zh: 鼎正直不阿，人有過，必面詆之。

translations.literal: Ding was upright and would not flatter; when someone had a fault he would invariably denounce it to his face.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was upright and unyielding: whenever anyone erred, he would rebuke him to his face.

sentences.zh: 壽隆初，升觀書殿學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shoulong he was promoted to Academician of the Hall for Viewing Books.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shoulong era he was promoted to Academician of the Hall for Viewing Books.

sentences.zh: 一日宴主第，醉與客忤，怨上不知己，坐是下吏。

translations.literal: One day at a feast in the princess's residence he became drunk and clashed with a guest; he resented that the emperor did not recognize his worth, and for this was sent down to the officials for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: One day at a feast in the princess's residence he grew drunk and quarreled with a guest, complaining that the emperor did not know his worth; for this he was handed over to the magistrates.

sentences.zh: 狀聞，上大怒，杖黥奪官，流鎮州。

translations.literal: When the report reached the throne, the emperor was greatly angered; he was beaten, tattooed, and stripped of office, and exiled to Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached the throne the emperor flew into a rage: Ding was beaten, tattooed, stripped of office, and exiled to Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 居數歲，有赦，鼎獨不免。

translations.literal: After several years there was an amnesty, but Ding alone was not included.
translations.idiomatic: After several years an amnesty was proclaimed, but Ding alone was not pardoned.

sentences.zh: 會守臣召鼎為賀表，因以詩貽使者，有「誰知天雨露，獨不到孤寒」之句。

translations.literal: It happened that the defending official summoned Ding to compose a congratulatory memorial; he therefore sent a poem to the envoy, containing the lines, "Who would have known heaven's rain and dew would alone not reach the solitary and cold?"
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the local commander summoned Ding to draft a congratulatory memorial, and he sent a poem to the envoy with the line, "Who knew heaven's rain and dew would pass the lonely and cold by alone?"

sentences.zh: 上聞而憐之，即召還，復其職。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he took pity on him and immediately recalled him, restoring him to his post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of it, took pity on him, and at once recalled him and restored his office.

sentences.zh: 乾統六年卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qiantong he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of the Qiantong reign.

sentences.zh: 鼎宰縣時，憩於庭，俄有暴風舉臥榻空中。

translations.literal: When Ding was magistrate of a county, he rested in the courtyard; suddenly a violent wind lifted his couch into the air.
translations.idiomatic: While Ding was serving as county magistrate he was resting in the courtyard when suddenly a violent wind lifted his couch into the air.

sentences.zh: 鼎無懼色，但覺枕榻俱高，乃曰：「吾中朝端士，邪無干正，可徐置之。

translations.literal: Ding showed no sign of fear; he only felt that both pillow and couch had risen, and said, "I am an eminent scholar of the central court; evil spirits do not dare interfere with what is upright—you may set me down slowly."
translations.idiomatic: Ding showed no fear; he only felt pillow and couch rising together, and said, "I am an upright scholar of the central court. Evil dare not touch what is correct—set me down gently."

sentences.zh: 」須臾，榻復故處，風遂止。

translations.literal: In a moment the couch returned to its former place and the wind ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment the couch returned to its place and the wind died away.

sentences.zh: 耶律昭，字述寧，博學，善屬文。

translations.literal: Yelü Zhao, style name Shuning, was learned and skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Zhao, courtesy name Shuning, was broadly learned and skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 統和中，坐兄國留事，流西北部。

translations.literal: In the Tonghe era he was implicated in his elder brother Guoliu's affair and exiled to the northwestern region.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tonghe era he was implicated in his elder brother Guoliu's case and exiled to the northwest.

sentences.zh: 會蕭撻凜為西北路招討使，愛之，奏免其役，禮致門下。

translations.literal: It happened that Xiao Talin became Commissioner for Subjugation of the Northwestern Circuit; he took a liking to Zhao, memorialized to exempt him from corvée labor, and received him with ceremony at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Talin became Commissioner for Subjugation of the Northwestern Circuit, he took a liking to Zhao, memorialized to free him from corvée, and received him with full courtesy at his gate.

sentences.zh: 欲召用，以疾辭。

translations.literal: When Talin wished to summon him to office, he declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Talin wished to summon him to office, he declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 撻凜問曰：「今軍旅甫罷，三邊宴然，惟阻卜伺隙而動。

translations.literal: Talin asked, "Now that military campaigns have just ceased and the three frontiers are tranquil, only the Zubu watch for openings and stir."
translations.idiomatic: Talin asked him, "Campaigns have only just ended and the three frontiers are quiet, yet the Zubu alone watch for openings and stir."

sentences.zh: 討之則路遠難至，縱之則邊民被掠，增戍兵則饋餉不給，欲茍一時之安，不能終保無變。

translations.literal: If we strike them the roads are long and hard to reach; if we indulge them the frontier people suffer plunder; if we increase garrison troops the supply of provisions cannot be met; seeking a moment's peace for the time being, we cannot in the end guarantee that nothing will change.
translations.idiomatic: To strike them is to face roads too long to reach; to indulge them is to let frontier people be plundered; to add garrison troops is to outrun our supplies. Seeking a moment's peace now, we cannot in the end be sure nothing will change.

sentences.zh: 計將安出？

translations.literal: What plan should we adopt?
translations.idiomatic: What plan should we adopt?

sentences.zh: 」昭以書答曰：

translations.literal: Zhao answered in a letter:
translations.idiomatic: Zhao answered in a letter:

sentences.zh: 竊聞治得其要，則仇敵為一家；

translations.literal: I have heard that when government grasps its essentials, even enemies become one household;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when governance grasps what matters, even enemies become one household;

sentences.zh: 失其術，則部曲為行路。

translations.literal: when it loses the method, even one's own followers become strangers on the road.
translations.idiomatic: when it loses the method, even one's own followers become strangers on the road.

sentences.zh: 夫西北諸部，每當農時，一夫為偵候，一夫治公田，二夫給糺官之役，大率四丁無一室處。

translations.literal: Among the tribes of the northwest, whenever the farming season comes, one man serves as scout, one man cultivates public fields, and two men supply corvée for the supervisory official—in general four adult males have not one household room to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: Among the northwestern tribes, whenever farming season comes one man serves as scout, one tends the public fields, and two supply corvée to the supervisory official—in general four able-bodied men have not a single room for the household.

sentences.zh: 芻牧之事，仰給妻孥。

translations.literal: For mowing and herding they depend entirely on their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Cutting fodder and tending herds they rely entirely on wives and children.

sentences.zh: 一遭寇掠，貧窮立至。

translations.literal: Once raided by bandits, poverty appears at once.
translations.idiomatic: A single raid and poverty follows at once.

sentences.zh: 春夏賑恤，吏多雜以糠比，重以掊克，不過數月，又復告困。

translations.literal: Spring and summer relief grain is often adulterated by officials with chaff; on top of this come extortion and squeezing—within no more than a few months they petition distress again.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and summer relief is often adulterated with chaff by officials, and on top of that comes extortion—within a few months they are begging relief again.

sentences.zh: 且畜牧者，富國之本。

translations.literal: Moreover pastoral herding is the foundation of a wealthy state.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, pastoral herding is the foundation of national wealth.

sentences.zh: 有司防其隱沒，聚之一所，不得各就水草便地。

translations.literal: The authorities guard against concealment and herd everything into one place, not allowing each to go to convenient pastures and water.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities guard against concealment and herd everything into one place, not letting each family reach convenient pasture and water.

sentences.zh: 兼以逋亡戍卒，隨時補調，不習風土，故日瘠月損，馴至耗竭。

translations.literal: Coupled with deserters from the garrisons who are replaced at any time and do not accustom themselves to local conditions, day by day they weaken and month by month they decline, gradually reaching exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Coupled with garrison deserters replaced at any moment who do not learn local conditions, they weaken day by day and month by month until exhaustion sets in.

sentences.zh: 為今之計，莫若振窮薄賦，給以牛種，使遂耕獲。

translations.literal: For the policy of today, nothing is better than reviving the destitute and lightening taxes, providing cattle seed so that they may complete plowing and harvest.
translations.idiomatic: For policy today, nothing is better than reviving the destitute, lightening taxes, and providing cattle seed so they can farm and harvest.

sentences.zh: 置遊兵以防盜掠，頒俘獲以助伏臘，散畜牧以就便地。

translations.literal: Station mobile troops to guard against looting, distribute captives to assist with seasonal sacrifices, and scatter pastoral herds to reach convenient locales.
translations.idiomatic: Station mobile troops against looting, distribute captives to help with seasonal rites, and scatter herds to convenient pasture.

sentences.zh: 期以數年，富強可望。

translations.literal: Within a few years strength and prosperity may be hoped for.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years strength and prosperity may be expected.

sentences.zh: 然後練簡精兵，以備行伍，何守之不固，何動而不克哉？

translations.literal: Then drill and select crack troops to fill the ranks—what defense will not be firm, what movement will not overcome?
translations.idiomatic: Then drill and select crack troops to fill the ranks—what defense would not hold, what campaign would not succeed?

sentences.zh: 然必去其難制者，則余種自畏。

translations.literal: Yet one must remove those difficult to control, and the remaining tribes will themselves fear.
translations.idiomatic: Yet one must remove those hard to control, and the remaining tribes will themselves submit in fear.

sentences.zh: 若舍大而謀小，避強而攻弱，非徒虛費財力，亦不足以威服其心。

translations.literal: If one abandons the large to scheme at the small, avoiding the strong to attack the weak, not only is wealth and effort spent in vain—it is also insufficient to overawe their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: If one abandons the large to scheme at the small, avoiding the strong to strike the weak, not only is wealth wasted—it is also insufficient to overawe their hearts.

sentences.zh: 此二者，利害之機，不可不察。

translations.literal: These two points are the pivot of advantage and harm and cannot fail to be examined.
translations.idiomatic: These two points are the pivot of advantage and harm and must be weighed with care.

sentences.zh: 昭聞古之名將，安邊立功，在德不在眾。

translations.literal: Zhao has heard that famous generals of antiquity who pacified the frontier and won merit did so through virtue and not through numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao has heard that famous generals of old who pacified the frontier and won merit did so through virtue, not through numbers.

sentences.zh: 故謝玄以八千破苻堅百萬，休哥以五隊敗曹彬十萬。

translations.literal: Thus Xie Xuan with eight thousand defeated Fu Jian's million, and Xiuge with five detachments defeated Cao Bin's hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Xie Xuan with eight thousand routed Fu Jian's million, and Xiuge with five detachments defeated Cao Bin's hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 良由恩結士心，得其死力也。

translations.literal: This was truly because kindness won the soldiers' hearts and secured their utmost strength unto death.
translations.idiomatic: This was because kindness won the soldiers' hearts and secured their strength unto death.

sentences.zh: 閣下膺非常之遇，專方面之寄，宜遠師古人，以就勛業。

translations.literal: Your Lordship has received an extraordinary appointment and bears sole trust for the region; you ought to take the ancients as teachers from afar to complete your achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Your Lordship has received an extraordinary appointment and bears sole trust for the region; you ought to take the ancients as your teachers from afar and complete your achievements.

sentences.zh: 上觀乾象，下盡人謀；

translations.literal: Observe above the signs of heaven, exhaust below the schemes of men;
translations.idiomatic: Observe above the signs of heaven and exhaust below the schemes of men;

sentences.zh: 察地形之險易，料敵勢之虛實。

translations.literal: examine the difficulty or ease of terrain and estimate the emptiness or fullness of enemy strength.
translations.idiomatic: discern the difficulty or ease of terrain and gauge the emptiness or fullness of enemy strength.

sentences.zh: 慮無遺策，利施後世矣。

translations.literal: Let no stratagem be omitted and benefits will extend to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Let no stratagem be omitted, and benefits will extend to later generations.

sentences.zh: 撻凜然之。

translations.literal: Talin was deeply impressed.
translations.idiomatic: Talin was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 開泰中，獵於拔裏堵山，為羯羊所觸，卒。

translations.literal: In the KaiTai era, while hunting on Mount Balidu, he was butted by a ram and died.
translations.idiomatic: During the KaiTai era, while hunting on Mount Balidu, he was butted by a ram and died.

sentences.zh: 劉輝，好學善屬文，疏簡有遠略。

translations.literal: Liu Hui loved learning and was skilled at composition, plain and sparing in manner, with far-reaching vision.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hui loved learning and was skilled at literary composition; plain in manner, he possessed far-reaching vision.

sentences.zh: 大康五年，第進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dakang he placed in the jinshi examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Dakang reign he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 大安末，為太子洗馬，上書言：「西邊諸番為患，士卒遠戍，中國之民疲於飛挽，非長久之策。

translations.literal: At the end of Da'an he served as Mentor of the Crown Prince and submitted a memorial saying: "The various tribes of the western frontier are a source of trouble; soldiers are garrisoned far away and the people of the Central Plains wear themselves out hauling supplies—this is no long-term policy.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Da'an era he served as Mentor of the Crown Prince and memorialized the throne: "The western tribes are a constant trouble; troops are garrisoned far away while the people of the Central Plains wear themselves out hauling supplies—this is no lasting policy.

sentences.zh: 為今之務，莫若城於鹽濼，實以漢戶，使耕田聚糧，以為西北之費。

translations.literal: The urgent task of the day is none better than fortifying cities at the salt marshes, filling them with Han households so that they farm fields and store grain as expenses for the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: The urgent task today is to build fortified towns at the salt marshes, settle them with Han households, and have them farm and store grain to supply the northwest.

sentences.zh: 」言雖不行，識者韙之。

translations.literal: Though his words were not adopted, those with insight approved them.
translations.idiomatic: Though his proposal was not adopted, men of insight approved it.

sentences.zh: 壽隆二年，復上書曰：「宋歐陽修編《五代史》，附我朝於四夷，妄加貶訾。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shoulong he again submitted a memorial saying: "The Song man Ouyang Xiu compiled the History of the Five Dynasties and placed our dynasty among the four barbarians, adding reckless denigration.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shoulong he again memorialized the throne: "The Song scholar Ouyang Xiu compiled the History of the Five Dynasties and placed our dynasty among the four barbarians, recklessly denigrating us.

sentences.zh: 且宋人賴我朝寬大，許通和好，得盡兄弟之禮。

translations.literal: Moreover the Song people rely on the magnanimity of our court, permitted to maintain friendship and accord, and attain the full observance of brotherly rites.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Song rely on our court's magnanimity, permitted friendship and peace, and enjoy the full observance of brotherly rites.

sentences.zh: 今反令臣下妄意作史，恬不經意。

translations.literal: Now they have turned instead to letting their subjects presumptuously compose histories, calm and heedless.
translations.idiomatic: Now they let their subjects presumptuously write history, calm and heedless of offense.

sentences.zh: 臣請以趙氏初起事跡，詳附國史。

translations.literal: Your servant requests that the Zhao clan's deeds at the founding be set forth in detail and appended to the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant requests that the Zhao clan's founding deeds be set forth in detail and appended to our national history.

sentences.zh: 」上嘉其言，遷禮部郎中。

translations.literal: The emperor commended his words and transferred him to Master of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his words and promoted him to Master of Rites in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 詔以賢良對策，輝言多中時病。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered a policy essay by men of talent; Hui's words largely hit the maladies of the age.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a policy examination for men of talent; Hui's answers largely struck the maladies of the age.

sentences.zh: 擢史館修撰，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Compiler in the Historiography Institute and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Compiler in the Historiography Institute and died.

sentences.zh: 耶律孟簡，字復易，於越屋質之五世孫。

translations.literal: Yelü Mengjian, style name Fuyi, was the fifth-generation descendant of Yuyue Wuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Mengjian, courtesy name Fuyi, was the fifth-generation descendant of the Yuyue Wuzhi.

sentences.zh: 父劉家奴，官至節度使。

translations.literal: His father Liu Jianu rose to the post of military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liu Jianu rose to the rank of military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 孟簡性穎悟。

translations.literal: Mengjian was by nature quick and perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: Mengjian was quick and perceptive by nature.

sentences.zh: 六歲，父晨出獵，俾賦《曉天星月詩》，孟簡應聲而成，父大奇之。

translations.literal: At six years old, when his father went out hunting at dawn and had him compose a poem on "Stars and Moon at Daybreak," Mengjian responded as soon as the words were spoken; his father was greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: At six, when his father went hunting at dawn and asked him to compose a poem on "Stars and Moon at Daybreak," Mengjian answered as soon as the words were spoken, and his father was astonished.

sentences.zh: 既長，善屬文。

translations.literal: When grown he was skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he became skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 大康初，樞密使耶律乙辛以奸險竊柄，出為中京留守，孟簡與耶律庶箴表賀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dakang, the Privy Councillor Yelü Yixin by treacherous craft usurped power and was sent out as Commissioner of the Central Capital; Mengjian together with Yelü Shuzhen submitted a congratulatory memorial.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Dakang, Privy Councillor Yelü Yixin seized power through treachery and was sent out as Commissioner of the Central Capital; Mengjian and Yelü Shuzhen submitted a congratulatory memorial.

sentences.zh: 未幾，乙辛復舊職，銜之，謫巡磁窯關。

translations.literal: Before long Yixin resumed his former post and bore a grudge; Mengjian was demoted to patrol duty at the Ciyao Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yixin returned to his former post and bore a grudge; Mengjian was demoted to patrol the Ciyao Pass.

sentences.zh: 時雖以讒見逐，不形辭色。

translations.literal: Though at the time he was driven out through slander, he showed no change in speech or countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Though driven out through slander, he showed no change in speech or countenance.

sentences.zh: 遇林泉勝地，終日忘歸。

translations.literal: When he came upon fine scenery of forest and spring he would forget to return all day.
translations.idiomatic: When he came upon fine scenery of forest and spring he would linger all day and forget to return.

sentences.zh: 明年，流保州。

translations.literal: The next year he was exiled to Baozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was exiled to Baozhou.

sentences.zh: 及聞皇太子被害，不勝哀痛，以詩傷之，作《放懷詩》二十首。

translations.literal: When he heard that the crown prince had been murdered he could not overcome his grief; he mourned him in verse and composed twenty poems entitled "Poems of Letting Go the Heart."
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that the crown prince had been murdered he was overcome with grief; he mourned him in verse and composed twenty poems entitled Poems of Letting Go the Heart.

sentences.zh: 自序云：「禽獸有哀樂之聲，螻蟻有動靜之形。

translations.literal: In his preface he wrote: "Beasts and birds have sounds of sorrow and joy; ants and insects have forms of movement and stillness.
translations.idiomatic: In his preface he wrote: "Beasts and birds have sounds of sorrow and joy; ants and insects have forms of movement and stillness.

sentences.zh: 在物猶然，況於人乎？

translations.literal: If it is so even among things, how much more among men?
translations.idiomatic: If it is so even among things, how much more among human beings?

sentences.zh: 然賢達哀樂，不在窮通禍福之間。

translations.literal: Yet for the worthy and penetrating, sorrow and joy lie not between poverty and success, fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for the worthy and penetrating, sorrow and joy do not depend on poverty or success, fortune or disaster.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：『樂天知命，故不憂。

translations.literal: The Classic of Changes says: 'Content with heaven and knowing fate, therefore without worry.'
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Changes says: 'Content with heaven and knowing fate, and therefore without worry.'

sentences.zh: 』是以顏淵簞瓢自得，此知命而樂者也。

translations.literal: Thus Yan Yuan with his bamboo basket was self-sufficient—this is knowing fate and being joyful.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Yan Yuan with his bamboo basket was self-sufficient—this is knowing fate and finding joy in it.

sentences.zh: 予雖流放，以道自安，又何疑耶？

translations.literal: Though I am in exile, I rest secure through the Way—what doubt remains?
translations.idiomatic: Though I am in exile, I rest secure through the Way—what doubt remains?

sentences.zh: 」大康中，始得歸鄉里。

translations.literal: In the Dakang era he was at last able to return to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dakang era he was at last able to return home.

sentences.zh: 詣闕上表曰：「本朝之興，幾二百年，宜有國史以垂後世。

translations.literal: He went to court and submitted a memorial saying: "Since our dynasty rose, it has been nearly two hundred years; there ought to be a national history to hand down to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: He went to court and submitted a memorial: "Since our dynasty rose, nearly two hundred years have passed; there ought to be a national history to hand down to posterity.

sentences.zh: 」乃編耶律曷魯、屋質、休哥三人行事以進。

translations.literal: Thereupon he compiled the career records of Yelü Helu, Wuzhi, and Xiuge and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he compiled the career records of Yelü Helu, Wuzhi, and Xiuge and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上命置局編修。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that a bureau be established for compilation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that a bureau be established for compilation.

sentences.zh: 孟簡謂余官曰：「史筆天下之大信，一言當否，百世從之。

translations.literal: Mengjian told the other officials: "The historiographer's brush is the great trust of the realm; whether a single word is right or wrong, a hundred generations will follow it.
translations.idiomatic: Mengjian told the other officials: "The historiographer's brush is the great trust of the realm; whether a single word is right or wrong, a hundred generations will follow it.

sentences.zh: 茍無明識，好惡徇情，則禍不測。

translations.literal: If there is no clear judgment and likes and dislikes follow private feeling, then disaster is unforeseeable.
translations.idiomatic: Without clear judgment, if likes and dislikes follow private feeling, disaster is unforeseeable.

sentences.zh: 故左氏、司馬遷、班固、范曄俱罹殃禍，可不慎歟！

translations.literal: Therefore Zuo Qiuming, Sima Qian, Ban Gu, and Fan Ye all suffered calamity—is caution not required!
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Zuo Qiuming, Sima Qian, Ban Gu, and Fan Ye all suffered calamity—is caution not required!

sentences.zh: 」乾統中，遷六院部太保。

translations.literal: In the Qiantong era he was transferred to Grand Protector of the Six Tribes Commission.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qiantong era he was transferred to Grand Protector of the Six Tribes Commission.

sentences.zh: 處事不拘文法，時多笑其迂。

translations.literal: In handling affairs he did not stick to written regulations; at the time many laughed at him as pedantic.
translations.idiomatic: In handling affairs he did not stick to written regulations; at the time many laughed at him as pedantic.

sentences.zh: 孟簡聞之曰：「上古之時，無簿書法令而天下治。

translations.literal: When Mengjian heard this he said: "In high antiquity there were no ledgers and laws yet the realm was governed.
translations.idiomatic: When Mengjian heard this he said: "In high antiquity there were no ledgers and laws, yet the realm was governed.

sentences.zh: 蓋簿書法令適足以滋奸幸，非聖人致治之本。

translations.literal: Ledgers and laws are just enough to breed crafty favor; they are not the foundation by which sages bring order.
translations.idiomatic: Ledgers and laws are just enough to breed crafty favor—they are not the foundation by which sages bring order.

sentences.zh: 」改高州觀察使，修學校，招生徒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner of Guozhou for Observation, built schools, and enrolled students.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Commissioner of Guozhou for Observation, built schools, and enrolled students.

sentences.zh: 遷昭德軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Zhaode Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Zhaode Army.

sentences.zh: 以中京饑，詔與學士劉嗣昌減價糶粟。

translations.literal: Because the Central Capital suffered famine, the emperor ordered that he together with Academician Liu Sichang sell grain at reduced price.
translations.idiomatic: When the Central Capital suffered famine, the emperor ordered him and Academician Liu Sichang to sell grain at reduced prices.

sentences.zh: 事未畢，卒。

translations.literal: Before the task was finished he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before the task was finished he died.

sentences.zh: 耶律谷欲，字休堅，六院部人。

translations.literal: Yelü Guyu, style name Xiujian, was a man of the Six Tribes Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Guyu, courtesy name Xiujian, was a man of the Six Tribes Commission.

sentences.zh: 父阿古只，官至節度使。

translations.literal: His father Aguozhi rose to the post of military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Aguozhi rose to the rank of military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 谷欲沖淡有禮法，工文章。

translations.literal: Guyu was mild and detached, observant of ritual propriety, and accomplished in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Guyu was mild and unassuming, observant of ritual propriety, and accomplished at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 統和中，為本部太保。

translations.literal: In the Tonghe era he served as Grand Protector of his native commission.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tonghe era he served as Grand Protector of his native commission.

sentences.zh: 開泰中，稍遷塌母城節度使。

translations.literal: In the KaiTai era he was gradually transferred to Military Commissioner of Tamucheng.
translations.idiomatic: During the KaiTai era he was gradually promoted to Military Commissioner of Tamucheng.

sentences.zh: 鞫霸州疑獄，稱旨，授啟聖軍節度使。

translations.literal: He investigated doubtful cases in Bazhou; his work pleased the emperor, and he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Qisheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: He investigated doubtful cases in Bazhou; his work pleased the emperor, and he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Qisheng Army.

sentences.zh: 太平中，復為本部太保。

translations.literal: In the Taiping era he again served as Grand Protector of his native commission.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiping era he again served as Grand Protector of his native commission.

sentences.zh: 謝病歸，俄擢南院大王。

translations.literal: He resigned on grounds of illness and returned home; shortly afterward he was promoted to King of the Southern Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on grounds of illness and returned home; shortly afterward he was promoted to King of the Southern Commission.

sentences.zh: 嘆風俗日頹，請老，不許。

translations.literal: He lamented that customs daily declined and requested retirement, but permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He lamented that customs were daily in decline and asked to retire, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 興宗命為詩友，數問治要，多所匡建。

translations.literal: Emperor Xingzong appointed him a poetry companion and frequently asked him about essentials of governance; he offered much corrective counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xingzong made him a poetry companion and often asked him about essentials of governance; he offered much corrective counsel.

sentences.zh: 奉詔與林牙耶律庶成、蕭韓家奴編遼國上世事跡及諸帝《實錄》，未成而卒，年九十。

translations.literal: By imperial order he together with Linya Yelü Shucheng and Xiao Hanjianu compiled the deeds of earlier Liao affairs and the Veritable Records of the various emperors; before completion he died, aged ninety.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he joined Linya Yelü Shucheng and Xiao Hanjianu in compiling the deeds of earlier Liao affairs and the Veritable Records of the various emperors; he died before the work was finished, at the age of ninety.

sentences.zh: 論曰：孔子言：「誦《詩》三百，授之以政，不達。

translations.literal: The discussion says: Confucius said, "One who has recited the three hundred Odes and is entrusted with government affairs yet does not succeed—
translations.idiomatic: The discussion says: Confucius said, "If one has recited the three hundred Odes yet, when entrusted with government, does not succeed—

sentences.zh: 雖多，亦奚以為？

translations.literal: however many he has recited, of what use are they?"
translations.idiomatic: however many he has recited, of what use are they?"

sentences.zh: 」王鼎忠直達政，劉輝侍青宮，建言國計，昭陳邊防利害，皆洞達闿敏。

translations.literal: Wang Ding was loyal and upright and mastered statecraft; Liu Hui attended the Eastern Palace and offered counsel on national policy; Zhao set forth the advantages and harms of frontier defense—all were penetrating and quick in understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ding was loyal, upright, and mastered statecraft; Liu Hui served the crown prince and offered counsel on national policy; Zhao set forth the advantages and harms of frontier defense—all were penetrating and quick of understanding.

sentences.zh: 孟簡疾乙辛奸邪，黜而不怨。

translations.literal: Mengjian detested Yixin's treachery and wickedness; though dismissed he bore no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Mengjian detested Yixin's treachery; though dismissed, he bore no resentment.

sentences.zh: 孰謂文學之士，無益於治哉！

translations.literal: Who would say that men of letters are of no benefit to governance!
translations.idiomatic: Who would say that men of letters are of no benefit to governance!
